question.problem: Evaluate $\sin \left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$ by converting the angle to degrees.
question.worked_solution:
First, we convert $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ radians to an equivalent measure in degrees. This gives

$$
\left(\dfrac{\pi} 6\right) \left(\dfrac {180^\circ} {\pi}\right) = \dfrac {180^\circ} {6} = 30^\circ.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\sin \left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \sin 30^\circ.
$$

Finally, since we know that $\sin 30^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2},$ we obtain

$$
\sin\left( \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)  = \dfrac{1}{2}.
$$
